title: Ganges Water Sharing Treaty
subtitle: India and Bangladesh signed a 30-year dry-season water-sharing treaty at Farakka on 12 December 1996.
summary: On 12 December 1996, Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and India Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda signed the Treaty on Sharing of the Ganga/Ganges Waters at Farakka in New Delhi. The treaty set a formula for sharing flows during the lean season, 1 January–31 May, using ten-day periods and measured flow at Farakka. It entered into force on signature for 30 years, with provision for review and adjustment and a commitment to cooperate on other shared rivers.
heroTagline: A 30-year India–Bangladesh agreement set rules for sharing Ganges flows at Farakka.
whyItMatters: The treaty created a formal bilateral mechanism for sharing lean-season flows of a transboundary river. Its formula, review provisions and commitment to negotiate agreements on other common rivers made it an important framework for India–Bangladesh water diplomacy.

claimCitations.claim: On 12 December 1996, Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and India Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda signed the Treaty on Sharing of the Ganga/Ganges Waters at Farakka in New Delhi. The treaty set a formula for sharing flows during the lean season, 1 January–31 May, using ten-day periods and measured flow at Farakka. It entered into force on signature for 30 years, with provision for review and adjustment and a commitment to cooperate on other shared rivers.

The treaty created a formal bilateral mechanism for sharing lean-season flows of a transboundary river. Its formula, review provisions and commitment to negotiate agreements on other common rivers made it an important framework for India–Bangladesh water diplomacy.
The treaty established a 30-year framework for seasonal Ganges water sharing and a bilateral process for review, monitoring and possible adjustment.
The agreement is a prominent example of Bangladesh and India addressing a shared-river issue through a negotiated treaty and continuing joint mechanisms.
